History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ yo woman with ESLD ___ hep C complicated by 
___ on the transplant list with MELD 22 presenting with mental 
status changes and hemiparesis.  
.  
She reports being recently incontinent of urine for 3 weeks and 
feeling more cloudy for the past week. Three days prior to 
admission she began forgetting things and was very much worse 
than her baseline (lives alone, does all of own ADLs, drives). 
On the day of admission her niece found her slurring her speech, 
not making sense. Per the niece, she was walking normally with 
not evidence of weakness but was incontinent of urine. She was 
brought to the ED.  
.  
Apart from the above, the patient's niece is not aware of any 
recent illnesses, fevers, diarrhea, or other complaints. She did 
not eat or drink anything today.  
.  
In the ED, initial VS were: 99.2 rectal 129/63 78 16 99% RA. She 
suffered a generalized tonic-clonic seizure while in the 
emergency room; convulsions resolved after 2 minutes with 
administration of ativan 2mg IV. It was noted that she had a 
left gaze preference prior to and during her seizure; she had a 
left-sided hemiparesis after the seizure. Neurology was 
consulted and was concerned about the focal component of her 
seizures. CT Head was negative per radiology, although the neuro 
resident was concerned about possible hyperdensity in the right 
occipital lobe. The patient was given ceftriaxone and vancomycin 
at meningitis doses but LP was not done because of her 
coagulopathy. Tox screen and cultures were sent and she was 
admitted to the liver service for further care.  
.  
Upon acceptance to the medicine service, she was answering all 
questions appropriately. She denied pain, headache, neck 
stiffness, photophobia. Review of systems was otherwise 
negative.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ with hep C cirrhosis (on the transplant list 
with MELD 19) and ___ admitted for mental status changes and 
seizure.  
.  
# Seiuzure: This was her first seizure with no clear inciting 
event. Per report, the seizure was initially focal with 
left-ward gaze and ? left hemiparesis after the event. Head CT 
was negative for any acute process. Differential included 
metabolic cause, brain lesion (possibly HCC metastasis), 
ischemia, infection.  She was loaded with Keppra in the ED and 
continued on this medication.  Electrolytes were aggresively 
repleted.  During the 24 hours after the seizure, she was 
somewhat slow and tired but gradually came back to her baseline. 
 She was unable to tolerate an MRI initially, but later agreed 
to the test and it did not show any acute inracranial process.  
EEG showed moderate to severe diffuse encephalopathy but no 
epileptiform discharges. LP was done on ___ (after had 
received antibiotics) and was negative for infection. 
Ceftriaxone and vancomycin were initially started for concern 
for infection but blood cx were no growth and urine cx returned 
as Klebsiella Pneumoniae sensitive to Bactrim so was continued 
on this medication through ___. She also received acyclovir 
initially for possible HSV encephalitis but this was 
discontinued due to low clinical suspicion. She did well off Abx 
and MS continued to improve. She was seen by neuro and loaded 
with keppra and started on 500mg BID increased q 4 days. She was 
on 750mg BID at time of discharge. She should increase to 1000mg 
PO BID on ___. She remained afberile throughout hospital 
course. 
.  
# Mental status changes: Although the slowing noted during her 
first day in the hospital likely represented post-ictal state, 
the incontinence and increasing confusion prior to her seizure 
was concerning for intracranial process (e.g. tumor or 
infection), systemic infection, or hepatic encephalopathy. Tox 
screen was negative.  Lactulose was started and MS improved. MRI 
and CT did not show any acute intracranial process but final 
read of MRI still pending at time of discharge.  
.  
# ESLD/___: MELD on admission was 19.  Outpatient doses of 
propranolol and spironolactone were continued.  Abdominal US 
showed a suspicious lesion previously noted on CT that was 
approx 2cm. CT was repeated and showed no change in lesion 
(approx. 1.7x1.8cm) from ___. 
.  
# Hyperglycemia: Despite having no history of diabetes. Pt had 
___ in high 200s to 300s. She was started on insulin regimen 
(lantus and HISS) which was uptitrated. At time of discharge she 
was discharged on insulin ___ BID with HISS. ___ was 
consulted and recommended treating pt as Type 1 intially. Anti 
islet cell, insulin, GAD antibodies and C peeptide were sent and 
were still pending.     
.
# Hyponatremia: Pt initially had hyponatremia 133 which 
resolved. 
.  
# Anemia: Patient noted to have downward trending HCT throughout 
hospital course from 30 to approx ___. She had trace guaiac 
positive stool. HCT was repeated and was. Iron studies were 
normal. Hemolysis labs showed slightly elevated LDH which was 
stable, slightly low haptoglobin which may have been secondary 
to transfusion of FFP.
.
# Coagulopathy: Platelets and INR were at baseline. She was 
given plt and FFP prior to LP.  
.  
# GERD:  PPI was continued
. 
# Osteopenia:  Vitamin D and calcium were continued

radiology_notes.text:
NON-CONTRAST HEAD CT.

Comparison made with a prior study from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with left-sided weakness, change in
mental status and left gaze preference.  History of severe liver disease.
Evaluate for bleed or infarct.

FINDINGS:  Non-contrast head CT.  There is no intra-axial or extra-axial
hemorrhage, shift of normally midline structures, hydrocephalus, or evidence
of major vascular territorial infarction.  Mild periventricular white matter
hypodensity is likely related to chronic microvascular ischemic disease. Areas
of basal ganglial calcification are again noted.  Paranasal sinuses, mastoid
air cells, and middle ear cavities are well aerated.  There is no evidence of
skull fracture.  Surrounding soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

No acute intracranial process.

PORTABLE CHEST RADIOGRAPH

Comparison is made with a prior study from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with mental status change.  Evaluate for
pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  Portable AP upright chest radiograph is obtained.  Multiple
overlying EKG wires and low lung volumes limit evaluation.  There is vague
increased opacity at the lateral lung bases bilaterally, which when compared
with prior study may reflect an element of scarring.  No definite evidence of
pneumonia, CHF, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax is seen.  Cardiomediastinal
silhouette appears grossly stable.  Osseous structures appear intact.

IMPRESSION:

Vague scarring at the lung bases bilaterally.  No evidence of pneumonia or
CHF.

MRI SCAN OF THE BRAIN

HISTORY:  Hepatitis C cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, admitted with a
new tonic-clonic seizure and focal component with mental status changes.
Evaluate for seizure focus.

TECHNIQUE:  Only a sagittal T1 weighted scan series was of acceptable scan
quality.  Attempted axial T1-weighted images as well as time-of-flight imaging
of the circle of ___ were all uninterpretable due to gross patient motion.

FINDINGS:  Within the limitations of this very restricted scans series, there
does not appear to be evidence for hydrocephalus or overt shift of the
normally midline structures.  However, there is a elevated T1 signal seen
within the lentiform nuclei bilaterally, which likely is a reflection of the
known hepatic dysfunction.  The sagittal scan suggests slight prominence of
the upward convex curvature of the pituitary gland.  Given the very limited
imaging available at this time, a small adenoma cannot be excluded, although
the pituitary gland does not appear to exhibit suprasellar extension.  There
is no compression of the adjacent optic chiasm.

CONCLUSION:  Incomplete study, as noted above.

INDICATION:  ___ female patient, with hepatitis C cirrhosis and
hepatocellular carcinoma, admitted with new seizures, with focal competent in
mental status changes, to evaluate for focus of seizures, question
hyperdensity in the right parieto-occipital lobe on CT ___.

COMPARISON:  CT of the ___ done on ___ and incomplete MR ___ done on
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted imaging of the brain was performed
without IV contrast.  3D TOF MR angiogram of the ___ was performed with MIP
reformations.  IV contrast was not administered, as the patient could not lie
still.

FINDINGS:

MRI OF THE BRAIN:

As ___ the prior study, the basal ganglia on both sides have T1
hyperintense appearance which can relate to the known hepatic dysfunction;
along with small susceptibility foci related to mineralization.
The pituitary gland has a superior convex border but is less than 1cm in
___.
On the axial FLAIR sequence, there are scattered FLAIR hyperintense foci in
the cerebral white matter on both sides, in the frontal and the parietal
lobes, without associated abnormal susceptibility or restricted diffusion. The
ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are normal. The major vascular arterial
flow voids are noted.  The visualized portions of the paranasal sinuses are
clear.

The hippocampi are slightly small and asymmetric, with the left side being
smaller than the right.

3D TOF MR ANGIOGRAM OF THE ___:

The major intracranial arteries, without focal flow-limiting stenosis,
occlusion, or aneurysm more than 3 mm within the resolution of MR angiogram.
Atherosclerotic contour irregularity and some stenosis is noted in the
cavernous segments of internal carotid arteries. However, no flow limitation
is noted.

Slightly prominent appearance of the A2 segment of the right anterior cerebral
artery can relate to a small infundibulum at the junction of the A1 and A2
segments. There is fetal PCA pattern on the right side.


IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intracranial abnormality.

2.  Nonspecific FLAIR hyperintense foci in the cerebral white matter on both
sides, can relate to sequelae of chronic small vessel occlusive disease.

3.  Patent major intracranial arteries without focal flow-limiting stenosis,
occlusion, or aneurysm more than 3 mm within the resolution of MR angiogram.
Evidence of atherosclerotic disease, without flow-limiting stenosis is noted
in the cavernous segments.  Small hippocampi as described above on both sides.
Pl. see other details above.

with cirrhosis.  1.5 x 2.1 x 1.8 cm hyperechoic lesion adjacent to the IVC
likely corresponds to the suspicious lesion seen in segment ___ of the liver

gallbladder is filled with stones.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic

IMPRESSION:
1.  2 cm hyperechoic lesion in the liver adjacent to the IVC likely
corresponds to the suspicious lesion seen in segment IV A of the liver on CT
from ___.
2.  Nodular and shrunken contour of the liver consistent with cirrhosis.
3.  Cholelithiasis without evidence of cholecystitis.
4.  Patent portal vein.

INDICATION:  Hepatitis C, cirrhosis, and history of liver lesion.

COMPARISON:  CTA abdomen performed ___ and MRI abdomen performed ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired images were obtained through the abdomen before and
then after the uneventful administration of 130 cc of IV Optiray contrast in
multiple phases.

FINDINGS:  There is a stable 3-mm pulmonary nodule in the right middle lobe.
Small bilateral effusions, right greater than left are associated with
compression atelectasis.  Heart size is top normal.  There is no pericardial
effusion. Coronary artery and aortic valve atherosclerosis is unchanged.

CT ABDOMEN:  An arterially enhancing lesion measuring 1.6 x 1.8 cm located at
the junction of segment VIII and segment ___ is unchanged since ___. The
lesion demonstrates washout and pseudocapsular enhancement on delayed images.
Although this is unchanged since ___, this remains highly suspicious for
hepatocellular carcinoma. The portal venous and hepatic systems are patent. An
accessory right hepatic artery and a replaced left hepatic artery remain
patent. Nodular contour of the liver is unchanged.  No new lesion is
identified.

The kidneys demonstrate stable subcentimeter hypodensities which likely
represent cysts, although are too small to be characterized. The gallbladder
again demonstrates innumerable layering stones.  The pancreas unremarkable.
The spleen measures up to 11.6 cm in its longest dimension; a small
hypodensity is seen on only one phase and may be perfusion related. There is
slightly increased lymphadenopathy near the porta hepatis with the largest
node measuring 1.5 x 1.2 cm, which is slightly increased since ___.  The
imaged loops of large and small bowel are grossly unremarkable except some
stable post- surgical changes in the stomach.

Bone windows demonstrate no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No change in appearance of segment ___ junction liver lesion which
remains highly suspicious for hepatocellular carcinoma.  There is increased
portal lymphadenopathy as noted above.

2.  Stable pulmonary nodule in the right middle lobe.

3.  Cirrhosis with portal hypertension is unchanged. Small hypodensity in
spleen noted on one phase.

4.  Cholelithiasis without evidence of cholecystitis.

5.  Increased ascites.
